record.tier: 1 year plan, $3.99 per month billed annually ($47.88 per year); free version 3 GB per month

free_tier.stated: Free version: 'Unlimited VPN traffic, compared to 3 GB per month in the free version', up to 2 devices ('compared to only 2 in the free version') and fewer server locations. Paid: all locations, unlimited speed and traffic, up to 10 devices.
free_tier.notes: The free version needs an AdGuard account login (email, or Google, Apple or Facebook sign-in). The paid price cards: 1 month $11.99 per month, 1 year $3.99 per month billed annually, 2 years $2.99 per month billed every two years.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an exit address, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: No object is stored; the constraints are the free 3 GB per month and the device counts in limits.

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel and a rented exit address, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The vendor's privacy page says it does not collect logs on VPN servers; no byte retention applies.

egress.terms: Paid plans list 'Unlimited traffic' and 'Unlimited speed'; the free version is '3 GB per month'. No overage price exists because the paid plan is unmetered; no byte was counted through a tunnel.
egress.free_allowance: 3 GB per month on the free version

record.interface_detail: AdGuard VPN CLI (adguardvpn-cli) on Linux with a TUN mode and a SOCKS5 mode; apps for Windows, macOS, Android and iOS and browser extensions. The SOCKS5 mode is a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:1080 by default; the vendor documents no remote SOCKS5 endpoint with credentials.
record.tooling: The vendor's CLI on a Linux machine gives a local SOCKS5 proxy (TCP and UDP) that any client on that machine can use; the apps and extensions cover the other platforms. The CLI's protocol option is HTTP2, QUIC or automatic.
record.chaining: A compute node runs the CLI in SOCKS5 mode and sends requests to 127.0.0.1:1080, so they leave at the chosen location's address; a Worker cannot reach that loopback proxy, so it needs a node in front of it.

limits.value: Free version: '3 GB per month'; paid plans: 'Unlimited traffic'
10 simultaneous devices on paid plans, 2 on the free version

record.limits_note: Port forwarding and the BitTorrent rule are stated on no AdGuard VPN page read: unverified. Server locations on the paid plan are '75+' per the vendor home page.
record.binding_note: On the free version the 3 GB monthly traffic cap fails first; on the paid plan no byte quota is stated and the 10-device cap is the first stated limit. No rate was measured.

identity_cost.detail: An AdGuard account is needed even for the free version: 'first you need to log into your AdGuard account', by email or via Google, Apple ID or Facebook; 'We need your email address to register an AdGuard account and log you in.' A paid purchase takes an email address plus 'bank cards, PayPal, and cryptocurrency'. No phone number or identity document is asked on the pages read.

record.reliability_note: The 1 year card shows a struck-through $11.99 per month and a '-67%' badge, so the $3.99 may be a promotional rate that the page can change. unverified: no exit-IP registry class was measured.
record.confidence_note: Documented from the vendor's licence page, home page and knowledge base as served. Measured would need an account, a tunnel brought up in each mode and a byte count against the 3 GB free cap.
